messages:
devon: Heads up — eu-west1 showed a big NVMe IOPS spike, GPU attach latency shot up and many pods stuck provisioning.
infra-bot: [ALERT] cluster/eu-west1: local-nvme-iops > 850k over 5m, affected nodes: 12, impacted pods: gpu-provisioner (rate-limited)
kevin: seeing the same. repro steps: launch 50 small gpu jobs -> attach latency 2x, many fallbacks to preemptible.
maria: what's the root cause? scrub? janitor? overlayfs flush?
devon: looks like ephemeral-cleaner concurrency + nightly scrub overlapped with a customer batch. scrub + cleaner = sustained small random writes. iops distribution skewed.
tyler: propose an "IO circuit-breaker" on GPU provisioning so we stop new GPU attaches once local NVMe 1m p95 iops > threshold. reduces failed attaches and avoids cascading requeues.
kevin: sgtm. need to ensure we don't starve critical jobs. we should allow a bypass for SLA tenants.
anna: define thresholds + cooldowns. maybe: if p95_io > 600k for 1m -> tripped, stop new attaches for 2m; if > 800k -> 5m. backoff exponential.
devon: draft alert + simple policy (pseudo):
```
policy: io_circuit_breaker:
  scope: node-local
  metric: nvme_iops_p95
  trip: 600000
  trip_window: 60s
  cooldown: 120s
  bypass_tags: ["sla:enterprise", "dedicated"]
```
kevin: also need dashboard + evictions watch. can we route attaches to other regions instead of blocking? fallback routing may cost more.
maria: cost vs reliability tradeoff. fallback to other regions increases egress & cross-region attach time. but better than failed jobs.
tyler: rollout plan: canary in sandbox, then eu-west1 non-prod, then opt-in for prod tenants. also metric for blocked_attach_count.
infra-bot: [NOTIFICATION] created ticket INFRA-4721 and started a canary deploy job eu-west1-sandbox.
devon: I'll own the canary. will add the policy to provisioner with feature flag.
kevin: pls add a compact playbook for oncall to manually flip thresholds + bypass.
anna: note: ensure we monitor scrub start windows and avoid scheduling janitor/cleaner concurrently with big customer batches — longer-term fix.
maria: thanks. if canary looks good let's schedule a 2-week opt-in window for Dedicated tenants.
kevin: ack. timeline?
devon: canary today, roll to non-prod tomorrow, prod opt-in next Tues.
maria: :thumbsup:
